sections.heading: EIP-8253 and Glamsterdam Scope
sections.summary: EIP-8253 (nonce bump for 28 accounts) will not be added to Glamsterdam; it replaces the DFI'd EIP-7610 and will be considered for Hegota.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8253](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8253) was proposed at ACDT on Monday as a potential last-minute addition to Glamsterdam, replacing [EIP-7610](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7610) which was DFI'd after problems were found.
  - The EIP is mainnet-only (no-op on Hoodi and Sepolia), meaning bugs would not be caught on testnets.
- Toni reported that most clients were against inclusion at ACDT. Key concern: interaction with BAL (block access lists) requiring bumped accounts to appear in the access list.
- Decision: **Not added to Glamsterdam.** Jochem confirmed there is no security urgency; Hegota is fine.
- Jochem requested immediate SFI for Hegota, arguing EIP-7610 had been SFI'd for Glamsterdam and EIP-8253 is its replacement. His chat message drew broad agreement, but danceratopz and nixo questioned SFI vs CFI, and nixo noted that "status in one fork doesn't automatically confer status in a new fork, it has to go back through the ladder".
  - Ansgar deferred the formal status decision to the Hegota scoping block later in the call. It was never revisited, so EIP-8253 remains PFI for Hegota.
- Aside (chat): danceratopz said glamsterdam-devnet-10 ran decoupled consensus testing, unrelated to Glamsterdam scope ([ACDT #095](https://forkcast.org/calls/acdt/095/#t=1242)); [glamsterdam-devnet-11](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/glamsterdam-devnet-11) is the next short-lived devnet, launching Monday.

sections.heading: EIP-8411 Fast Payload Broadcast PFI Request
sections.summary: Kamil requested permission to PFI EIP-8411 for Hegota post-deadline; the decision will be made on ACDC next week.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8411](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12299) is a CL-side EIP for fast parallel payload propagation, replacing the earlier Blocks and Blobs EIP.
- Kamil Salakhiev described it as important in the context of higher gas limits and potentially quicker slots.
- Relevant links shared in chat: [Discord discussion](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1545447655759544330), [P2P call notes](https://forkcast.org/calls/p2p/008/), and [Csaba's research post](https://ethresear.ch/t/wen-fast-payload-broadcast-segment-code-push-pull-and-everything-in-between/25913).
- Decision deferred to ACDC next week, as this is a CL-layer change.

sections.heading: EIP-8141 Frame Transaction Headliner Decision
sections.summary: Frame Transaction (EIP-8141) was confirmed as a headliner for Hegota with no objections; spec iteration is still ongoing.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8141](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8141) was SFI'd at the previous call but never formally confirmed as a headliner.
- No objections were raised. Multiple client teams reacted positively in chat (Geth, Besu, Nethermind, ethrex).
- Decision: **EIP-8141 is a headliner for Hegota.** The exact spec may still iterate.

sections.heading: EIPs Not Part of Client Rankings
sections.summary: Ansgar enumerated EIPs excluded from the ranking list, covering already-SFI'd, meta, cross-layer, withdrawn, no-champion, and pending-status EIPs.
sections.body:
- Already SFI'd: EIP-8141 (Frame Transaction) — no further scoping discussion needed.
- Meta EIP (no separate inclusion decision): [EIP-8173](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8173) (Foundations of EVM Control Flow). A sibling EIP will be discussed separately.
- Cross-layer, to be discussed on ACDC: [EIP-8146](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8146) (Block Access List Sidecars) and [EIP-8237](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8237) (Independent CL/EL Sync).
- Withdrawn by proposer: [EIP-7686](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7686), [EIP-7971](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7971), [EIP-7973](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7973).
- No champion: [EIP-7609](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7609), [EIP-8058](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8058), [EIP-8268](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8268).
- [EIP-8360](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12073) (TCREATE): status still open — the agenda lists it as a placeholder for an ephemeral-contract solution. Maria said her understanding from the last ACDE was that it had been implicitly PFI'd; Milos volunteered to champion it, since the original proposer could not attend. Jochem added in chat that [EIP-4758](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4758) (Deactivate SELFDESTRUCT) cannot be done without it.
  - Ansgar committed to clarifying the status async and having it ready for the scoping discussion in two weeks.

sections.heading: Hegota Scoping Process and Forkcast Rankings Overview
sections.summary: All six EL client teams submitted rankings; 37 EIPs discussed today using forkcast aggregation, with DFI-first pass across five topical pages.
sections.body:
- Rankings received from Besu, Erigon, ethrex, Geth, Nethermind, and Reth. [Forkcast aggregation page](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/hegota/client-priority/?layer=EL&team=Besu%2CErigon%2CEthrex%2CGeth%2CNethermind%2CReth&only=1&group=category) shared.
- 37 EIPs for today (38 including TCREATE deferred to next call). EIPs grouped into 5 topical pages.
- Rough thresholds discussed: below 1.0 = auto-DFI candidate; 1.0–2.5 = discussion needed; above 2.5 = likely CFI.
- Process agreed: DFI pass first across all five pages, then CFI pass. In practice, time ran out before CFI decisions could be made.
- Łukasz suggested focusing discussion on outlier votes rather than full round-robin per EIP.
- Multiple participants praised the coordination process and forkcast tooling as a major improvement over previous forks.

sections.heading: Account Abstraction EIP DFIs
sections.summary: EIP-7819 (SETDELEGATE instruction) and EIP-7851 (Code-Controlled EOA Delegation) were DFI'd with no objections.
sections.body:
- Both EIPs had very low client rankings (below 1.0).
- No one spoke up in their defense.
- Decision: **DFI for both EIP-7819 and EIP-7851.**

sections.heading: EVM Features DFIs and Delays
sections.summary: Four low-ranked EVM EIPs DFI'd; EIP-7979 (call/return opcodes) delayed pending compiler team input; EIP-8163 (extension opcode) delayed pending L2/alt-L1 signals; EIP-7923 DFI'd.
sections.body:
- **DFI'd unanimously (0.0–0.8 rating):** EIP-2488 (deprecate CALLCODE), EIP-8219 (checked arithmetic opcodes), EIP-8182 (private ETH/ERC20 transfers), EIP-7645 (alias ORIGIN to SENDER).
- **EIP-7979 (call and return opcodes):** Greg Colvin made an impassioned case ([CFI request](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2211#issuecomment-5608915336)), noting that the EVM is essentially the only smart contract VM without call/return support and that this blocks control flow analysis, compilation, and formal verification. He also noted he is the last champion left of the original group. Multiple chat participants supported delaying the DFI decision. Lightclient and others suggested compiler teams (Solidity, Vyper) should be present to state whether they would integrate this.
  - Decision: **Delayed** — no decision today; compiler teams to be invited for next call.
- **EIP-7923 (linear page-based memory costing):** Charles (champion) argued for a modern virtual memory model. Nethermind rated it B (nice to have), but ethrex and others rated it DFI. Nethermind declined to commit to two weeks of prototyping.
  - Decision: **DFI**, with understanding it could be revisited if room appears.
- **EIP-8163 (reserve EXTENSION opcode):** Piotr explained the chicken-and-egg problem — L2s/alt-L1s need the commitment to begin research. Ansgar personally advocated delay; lightclient requested a list of L2s/alt-L1s that actively want the opcode, plus a sketch of how extension namespace conflicts would be avoided. Danno reported in chat that 0xAE appears to be unused across L2s and alt-L1s.
  - Decision: **Delayed** — champion must aggregate L2/alt-L1 interest signals by next call; default outcome is DFI.

sections.heading: EVM Pricing and State Gas DFIs and Delays
sections.summary: EIP-8188, EIP-8358, and EIP-8115 DFI'd; EIP-8372 (normalized state gas limit) not DFI'd, to be resolved alongside the better-supported EIP-8368.
sections.body:
- **EIP-8188 (last written block for accounts/slots) and EIP-8358 (net gas metering for account changes):** Both rated ~1.0 or lower. No one spoke up against DFI.
  - Decision: **DFI for both.**
- **EIP-8115 (batch priority fees at end of block):** Nethermind rated it A (helps parallel block building post-BAL). Geth (Marius) argued the complexity is not worth the benefit. Nethermind acknowledged it's "not a hill to die on."
  - Decision: **DFI.**
- **EIP-8372 (normalized state gas limit):** Extremely low client ratings overall, but Maria and Anders argued it may be needed if Glamsterdam's state gas economics turn out unbalanced. Maria described both EIP-8368 and EIP-8372 as simple one-time recalibrations of a variable, and asked for the decision on *both* to be deferred until Glamsterdam ships and demand response can be observed. Marius and Dragan explained client teams chose the simpler EIP-8368; they're open to reconsidering later if a real need shows up.
  - Anders' pre-call [comment on the agenda](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2211#issuecomment-5618928305) laid out EIP-8372's role.
  - Ansgar pushed back on deferring: he would rather CFI both now and reject later if unneeded, since leaving decisions pending for months makes the fork look lighter than it is. Anders agreed with CFI'ing both.
  - Decision: **EIP-8372 not DFI'd today** — it will be resolved alongside EIP-8368, which Ansgar noted has a lot of support and is a likely CFI. No CFI decisions were taken this call.

sections.heading: ZK EVM Preparation: EIP-8200 EVMification DFI
sections.summary: EIP-8200 (EVMification of precompiles) was DFI'd; clients agreed the idea has merit but is premature for Hegota pending benchmarks and ongoing competitions.
sections.body:
- Ben Adams noted a [competition](https://www.yukon.org/precompile) is producing increasingly fast formally-verified EVM bytecode replacements for precompiles like MODEXP, but results are not yet mature enough — "it needs time to brew."
- Greg Colvin agreed it should go to DFI while calling the idea generally good, but wanted performance measurements first: he could not make EVMified static control flow validation fast enough even with "absolutely heroic EVM programming," and the whole point of precompiles is performance.
- Justin Florentine (Besu) flagged the risk of being unable to revert to native precompile implementations later; Kevaundray clarified gas costing would prevent that.
- Ethrex (Iván) supported the EIP's goals (reducing prover attack vectors, simplifying ZKVM implementations) but acknowledged insufficient numbers and lack of broader client support.
- Lightclient asked when clients expect mandatory zkEVM on L1. Gary Schulte pointed out the strawmap lists it at fork k*; lightclient's own chat estimate was that k* is "probably 3.5-4 years away." Łukasz argued EVMification is not required for zkEVM, just nice to have for simplification.
- Decision: **DFI for Hegota**, with expectation it will be revisited for a future fork.

sections.heading: Delayed State Root and SSZ Execution Blocks DFIs
sections.summary: EIP-7862 (delayed state root) and EIP-7807 (SSZ execution blocks) both DFI'd; EIP-8304 (trustless log index) delayed after Geth/Besu discussion.
sections.body:
- **EIP-7862 (delayed state root):** Besu (Karim) argued it removes state root from the hot path, enabling computation between blocks. Nethermind (Łukasz) countered that state root is not a major bottleneck, especially post-BAL with parallel computation. Łukasz suggested revisiting with binary tries.
  - Decision: **DFI**, with possible revisit at a future fork or if Glamsterdam reveals unexpected load.
- **EIP-7807 (SSZ execution blocks):** ethrex rated it positively. Geth (Marius) and Reth (Dragan) argued the blast radius is huge (everything reading headers/blocks must change) while user benefit is low; current RLP-based proofs work. Nethermind cited scope and blast radius concerns.
  - Decision: **DFI.**
- **EIP-8304 (trustless log and transaction index):** Zsolt (Geth, author) argued it enables provable range queries over events — something impossible today — and opens paths for on-chain provability, native UTXOs, and L2 communication. Lightclient strongly supported it, drawing an analogy to FOCIL: trustlessness is a core property worth building even without current demand.
  - Besu (Justin Florentine) agreed to delay and engage with the proposal, asking for a case for why off-chain trusted indexing is insufficient.
  - Reth (Dragan) was open to delay but skeptical.
  - Nethermind rated it B and has an [external contributor PR](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/13269) prototyping it.
  - Decision: **Delayed** — Besu and Reth committed to engaging async over two weeks; default outcome remains DFI if no progress.
- **EIP-8094 (eth/vhash blob-aware mempool):** Csaba (author) agreed with DFI, noting most features were folded into sparse blob pool.
  - Decision: **DFI.**

sections.heading: Next Call Preparation and Process Expectations
sections.summary: Next ACDE in two weeks will prioritize CFI decisions for top-8 EIPs and resolve all delayed DFI decisions; clients asked to raise concerns async beforehand.
sections.body:
- No CFI decisions were made this call due to time constraints; all non-DFI'd EIPs remain PFI.
- For next call: CFI pass on the 8 highest-ranked EIPs (all ≥2.5, none with any team at DFI tier), DFI resolution for all delayed EIPs, and if time allows, discussion of borderline EIPs.
- Ansgar asked clients with negative ratings on highly-ranked EIPs to come prepared with clear positions on what would change their minds.
- Maria requested that client concerns be raised async before the call so champions can address them, avoiding another round of delays.
  - Ansgar endorsed this: concerns should be raised in the first week, with the second week for discussion, so positions are updated before the call.
- Ansgar expressed optimism that scoping can be completed before Devcon.
- Justin Florentine asked for the expectation to be posted on the next meeting agenda; Ansgar agreed.
